'''Le'Aufa'amulia Asenati Lole-Taylor'''<ref name="Taylor Electoral Commission 2008">{{cite web |last=Electoral Commission |title=Party Lists of Unsuccessful Registered Parties |url= http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2008/e9/html/e9_part3_2.html |work=2008 General Election – Official Result |accessdate=4 December 2011}}</ref> (born {{birth based on age as of date |17|1980|noage=1}}) is a former New Zealand politician. She was a member of the [[New Zealand House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] for the [[New Zealand First]] party from 2011 to 2014.

==Early life==
Born in [[Samoa]],<ref name="Taylor Radio Australia">
{{cite web|last=ABC International|title=NZ First MP second Pacific woman MP|url=http://www.radioaustralia.net.au/pacbeat/stories/201111/s3378865.htm|work=Radio Australia: Pacific Beat|accessdate=4 December 2011}}</ref> Taylor emigrated to New Zealand at the age of 17.<ref name="Taylor NZ First Manukau East">{{cite web|last=Taylor |first=Asenati |title=Profile |url=http://asenatitaylornewzealandfirst.org.nz/profile.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110925012342/http://asenatitaylornewzealandfirst.org.nz/profile.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 September 2011 |work=Asenati Talor: NZ First-Manukau East Electorate |accessdate=4 December 2011}}</ref> She served as chairperson of the Auckland City Pacific Islands Board<ref>{{cite web|last=Lole-Taylor|first=L.-A. A.|title=Statement to the Royal Commission on Auckland Governance by the Pacific Islands Board Auckland City |url=http://auckland.royalcommission.govt.nz/rccms.nsf/0/CC2573E80010C73BCC257443000C1E77/$file/000D56D2.pdf |work=Royal Commission on Auckland Governance – Submissions |publisher=Royal Commission on Auckland Governance |accessdate=4 December 2011}}</ref> and as a member of the Pacific Health Advisory Committee<ref>{{cite web |last=Auckland District Health Board |title=Community and Public Health Advisory Committee Minutes |url=http://www.adhb.govt.nz/downloads/minutes/commpubh/2010/Minutes%20CPHAC%2027%20January%202010.pdf |publisher=Auckland District Health Board |accessdate=4 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426020515/http://www.adhb.govt.nz/downloads/minutes/commpubh/2010/Minutes%20CPHAC%2027%20January%202010.pdf |archivedate=26 April 2012}}</ref> of the [[Auckland District Health Board]]. Prior to election to Parliament, Taylor worked as the Regional Advisor Pacific Northern Region for Rehabilitation and Reintegration Services at the [[Department of Corrections (New Zealand)|Department of Corrections]].<ref name="Taylor Dept of Corrections1">
{{cite web|last=Department of Corrections |title=Pacific leaders play part in rehabilitation |url=http://www.corrections.govt.nz/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/523433/CorrVolunteer_March_2011.pdf |work=Corr Volunteer |accessdate=4 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406094253/http://www.corrections.govt.nz/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/523433/CorrVolunteer_March_2011.pdf |archivedate=6 April 2012 }}</ref><ref name="Taylor Dept of Corrections2">
{{cite web|last=Department of Corrections |title=Pasifika history and culture an important part of rehabilitation |url=http://www.corrections.govt.nz/news-and-publications/media-releases/2010-media-releases/pasifika_history_and_culture_an_important_part_of_rehabilitation2.html |work=2010 Media Releases |accessdate=4 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406094323/http://www.corrections.govt.nz/news-and-publications/media-releases/2010-media-releases/pasifika_history_and_culture_an_important_part_of_rehabilitation2.html |archivedate=6 April 2012 }}
</ref>

She has three children and one stepson.<ref name="Taylor for local government">
{{cite web|last=Lole-Taylor |first=Asenati |title=Asenati Lole-Taylor running for local government |url=http://www.eventpolynesia.com/news&info/nz/galleryarchive/NZ2_page_gal23sep07.htm |work=Newsroom 23–29 September 2007 |accessdate=4 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120602205406/http://www.eventpolynesia.com/news%26info/nz/galleryarchive/NZ2_page_gal23sep07.htm |archivedate=2 June 2012 }}</ref> She holds the chiefly title ''Le'Aufa'amulia'' from the Samoan village of [[Falese'ela]].<ref name="y022">{{cite web |date=6 October 2014 |title=Lole-Taylor, Asenati |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/lole-taylor-asenati/ |access-date=30 July 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref>

==Political career==

Taylor ran for office on three occasions under the name Asenati Lole-Taylor. In 2007, she was an unsuccessful [[New Zealand Labour Party]] candidate in the Tamaki-Maungakiekie Ward in the [[Auckland City Council]] elections.<ref name="Taylor for local government" />

By the following year she had changed parties to [[New Zealand First]]. She contested the [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008 election]] in the [[Maungakiekie (New Zealand electorate)|Maungakiekie]] electorate, and was placed seventh on the party list, but the party won no seats. For the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 election]] she contested [[Manukau East]] and elected as the eighth-ranked candidate on the party list.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2011 |title=New Zealand First Endorses Pacific Leader |url=https://auckland.scoop.co.nz/2011/08/new-zealand-first-endorses-pacific-leader/ |access-date=30 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

As a member of parliament, Taylor was a member of the law and order committee until March 2012 and thereafter sat on the social services committee. From March 2012 until the end of her term she was the New Zealand First party spokesperson on corrections, ethnic affairs, Pacific Island affairs and social welfare, and the associate spokesperson on housing.<ref name="y022" /> A member's bill in Taylor's name, the Sentencing (Protection of Children from Criminal Offending) Amendment Bill, passed its first reading in September 2013 and was defeated in December 2014.<ref name="y276">{{cite web |date=7 November 2017 |title=Sentencing (Protection of Children from Criminal Offending) Amendment Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/03f5675e-2ebd-4820-bac5-78354075cd23 |access-date=30 July 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref>

In 2013, Taylor voted against the [[Marriage (Definition of Marriage) Amendment Act 2013|Marriage Amendment Bill]], which aimed to permit same sex marriage in New Zealand, with all of her fellow New Zealand First MPs.<ref>{{cite news |date=29 August 2012 |title=Marriage equality bill: How MPs voted |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10830383 |accessdate=29 September 2014 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>

After being demoted to the sixteenth position on the [[Party lists in the 2014 New Zealand general election#New Zealand First|New Zealand First party list]], Lole-Taylor failed to return to Parliament at the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]].<ref>{{cite press release |url= http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1408/S00438/new-zealand-first-party-list-2014.htm |title=New Zealand First List 2014 |publisher=New Zealand First |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |date=26 August 2014 |accessdate=26 August 2014}}</ref>

==After Parliament==

Following her demotion and subsequent failure to get re-elect Taylor has kept a low profile. Taylor came to prominence when it was found both she and her husband, Dennis Taylor, had illicitly accessed private data during their time working for the Department of Corrections. The access was found to be in regards to an elected official of the [[New Zealand First]] Party.  Records pertaining to drink driving offences committed by Marise Bishop, a former director on New Zealand First's board and Mana electorate chairwoman, were accessed from Corrections. Bishop believed Dennis Taylor's motivation was down to his wife's loyalty to fellow Samoan New Zealand First member Tim Manu who was active in the Mana electorate but with whom Bishop had fallen out with.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/nz-first-mps-husband-under-investigation/FFH3ULBPU2XMKDANM275UF7BWY/ | title=MP's husband under investigation | date=17 July 2014 }}</ref> Following the release of this information Taylor hinted she was contemplating a move to Australia and removed most of her social media presence, having been known for outspoken tweets during her time as an MP.<ref>{{cite web |title= Former MP Asenati Lole-Taylor Broke Rules by Accessing Records| date= 19 December 2014 | url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/64324897/former-mp-asenati-loletaylor-broke-rules-by-accessing-records |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] | accessdate= 31 January 2015 }}</ref>

In May 2015 Taylor left New Zealand despite a probe into the activities of her and her husband. They were believed to have left New Zealand in March.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/68219959/former-nz-first-mp-leaves-country-during-police-probe|title = Former NZ First MP leaves country during police probe|date = 2 May 2015}}</ref>
